items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Cottrell, myself and Lloyd Glenn. The pianist that was in my band.

ctx.x: That was later then. That is correct. Much later. That's when it was first recorded. Paul Gayton is the one that put it on. Then later on I got Camille Howard to play it but she played it in the wrong vein. She played it in the jump tempo and You Don't Love Me isn't a jump song. It was the theme song of the band. Cottrell, myself and Lloyd Glenn. The pianist that was in my band. He came after Freeman didn't he? Long after Freeman. Yes he came quite a while after Freeman. I think that, I'm not for sure I think…
You had a regular arranger for your band?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I had a very, very peculiar pianist... Lloyd Glenn... we'd come to these dance halls... we'd play without a piano

ctx.x: Oh, yes, I have worlds of scrapbooks. Do you want to get the picture to you? I think she got it. Okay. All right. Let's see. Well, back to business of just how you would get set up and everything. Did you ever have to rent pianos in those days?

No, usually the dance halls had them in there, but I had a very, very peculiar pianist. To me, he's one of the greatest, and you know who I'm referring to, Lloyd Glenn. And he was very picky about his pianos. And a lot of times we'd come to these dance halls, and the pianos were so low that we would have to tune up with the piano and change our whole way of playing. Because we couldn't reach the piano, or narrow to tune it. So if we tune with the piano, Lloyd Glenn would have to transpose maybe a tone or two…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: The only one that didn't drink that went there with us. I don't ever remember him drinking anything and the thing was Lloyd Glenn. ... All of us was there.

ctx.x: Well, listen, I want to ask you about guys in your band, but you don't have to mention who they did in what? Like going to Wakes, if you don't want to mention their names?

Well, that wasn't a matter about the names. Yeah, okay. Old Jimmy Johnson used to like to hit the bottle after we finished playing. And we were over in Pensacola. Some fella died, so the booker or somebody told us to be sure and go to where the Wakes was that happens was going to be there. So we all paid respect to the dead man. None of us knew who he was. Right in the back of the house where the man was laid out was where the happenings was and Jimmy Johnson was back there buying up the booze as fast as we could…
And you just, it was like publicity?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-09-18
items.q: It was. It was Lloyd Glenn's idea himself. ... the man that started most of it was Lloyd. Lloyd had a lot of slang words.

ctx.x: But to me, I never hear many records where the piano stands out over the saxophones. You know, with the saxes in the background. Well, that was a very unusual thing.
It was. It was Lloyd Glenn's idea himself.
Oh, I see. You would work it out together.
